solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Little hits made by devil infiltrating saints

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside, so the devil's letters go within the saints' letters

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for saints, plural of St
Old Nick is a familiar name for the Devil

explanation.surface: Small blows struck by a devil who has crept in among the saints.
explanation.definitionFit: Snicks are slight cuts or glancing touches, as when a cricket ball just clips the bat edge.

clue.text: A wag may hit home finally — after this?

definitions.text: A wag may hit home finally — after this?

indicators.note: something hit is knocked about, so the letters of the first three words are knocked into a new order
finally points to the closing letter of the word home

explanation.surface: A joker might crack a line about getting back home once this is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'hit' sits inside a phrase that sounds like 'hit home'. Rearranging A WAG MAY gives AWAYGAM, and E, the last letter of 'home', completes it. Read whole, the clue says the team heads home after playing away.
explanation.definitionFit: After a fixture played at the opponents' ground, the visiting team finally travels back to its own base.

clue.text: Church the French bishop thought highly of — conducted a Eucharist here?

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
le is the French masculine word for 'the'
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to rate someone is to think highly of them

explanation.surface: A French bishop well regarded by his church leads a service of Holy Communion.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing 'here?' only hints that the church in the wordplay is where the service took place.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest is said to celebrate Mass or Communion when leading the service.

clue.text: Anna has a number of such birds

definitions.text: Anna has a number of such
definitions.meaning: the anna was an old Indian coin worth twelve of a smaller copper coin
magpies are commonly shortened in this way

explanation.walkthrough: Anna is not a girl here but a former coin of British India, divided into twelve smaller units.
explanation.definitionFit: The pie was a small Indian coin, and pie is also an old name for the magpie.

clue.text: Yells when Stan's partner gets stuck in pits

indicators.note: being stuck in something means being lodged inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: yells and cries are both loud shouts
Oliver Hardy, known as Ollie, was Stan Laurel's comedy partner

explanation.surface: Shouting breaks out as Stan's comic partner gets trapped down a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal mines are commonly called pits, and a colliery is such a mine with its buildings.

clue.text: Revolutionary female who can stand the heat of the kitchen?

definitions.text: who can stand the heat of the kitchen?

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A rebellious woman who copes well under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'if you can't stand the heat, get out of the kitchen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional cook works daily in the hot kitchen, literally standing its heat.

clue.text: Area with system of belief that's left one unable to participate

indicators.note: a player unable to take part drops out, so these letters drop out of the word

parts.note: a religion is a system of faith and worship
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A district whose faith has left one person excluded.
explanation.definitionFit: Region and area are synonyms for a stretch of territory.

clue.text: Demoralised actors rusticated from Oxford?

parts.note: the cast is the set of actors in a production
a student rusticated or sent away from the university is said to be sent down

explanation.surface: Players dejected after being expelled from Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge, being 'down' means away from the university; rusticated students are sent down.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cast down is an idiom for being dispirited and dejected.

clue.text: I'm now involved with exec in American state

indicators.note: involved means tangled together, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone now working alongside an executive in a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: This southwestern territory joined the United States as its forty-seventh state in 1912.

clue.text: Girl attached to heartless Henry, wild animal

indicators.note: attached to puts the girl's name right after the other piece
losing the heart leaves only the outside letters of the name

parts.note: Ena is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl linked to a cold-hearted Henry turns out to be a wild beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The laughing scavenger of African plains is a wild carnivorous mammal.

clue.text: Modesty of military company head

parts.note: COY is the army abbreviation for company
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's shoreline names

explanation.surface: The humility of an army unit's commander.
explanation.walkthrough: Ness, a headland, appears in British place names such as Shoeburyness.
explanation.definitionFit: Coyness is shy reticence, a kind of bashful modesty.

clue.text: Supporting Socialists? It's felt to be foolish

indicators.note: a foolish arrangement is a silly one, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Backing socialism is thought to be silly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the political left means backing socialist parties and policies.

clue.text: Water essential to these activities

indicators.note: essential to means at the core of, so the letters lie within these words

explanation.surface: Water is vital to these pursuits.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocean is a great body of salt water.

clue.text: Slowing down later on land that's been churned up

indicators.note: churned up soil is turned over, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A tractor is slowing as it reaches ploughed ground.
explanation.definitionFit: In music this Italian direction tells players to gradually reduce speed.

clue.text: Finding a meaning in silence

parts.note: this describes understanding speech without hearing it, by watching mouth movements

explanation.walkthrough: Sounds like contemplation; actually a deaf person following speech by watching the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cannot hear makes sense of speech from the movements of a speaker's mouth.

clue.text: Barry Humphries type who does business?

definitions.meaning: Barry Humphries was the Australian comedian who played Dame Edna, a performer crossing gender
one who carries out a deal or transaction

explanation.walkthrough: Split 3+5, the word is a performer playing across genders, as Humphries did as Dame Edna Everage.
explanation.definitionFit: A party to a commercial deal is formally one who transacts; split differently, a cross-dressing performer.

clue.text: Group concealing explosive in paper

indicators.note: concealing means holding hidden inside, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a set is a group of things belonging together
HE is the abbreviation for high explosive

explanation.surface: A cell hiding a bomb inside a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A single piece of paper is called a sheet.

clue.text: Upsetting depression's overwhelming great man — one's not perfectly rounded

indicators.note: overwhelming means engulfing, so one piece surrounds the other
in a down clue upsetting means turning upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a dip is a depression in the ground; with the 's it becomes plural-like
a hero is a great man

explanation.surface: Low mood takes over a great figure, who is not quite all-round.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Upsetting' turns the plural depressions upside down; 'overwhelming' wraps that round the great man.
explanation.definitionFit: A spheroid is a body close to a sphere but not exactly round, like a slightly flattened globe.

clue.text: Greek character showing a very high level of acidity

definitions.meaning: a letter of the Greek alphabet, between upsilon and chi

definitions.text: a very high level of acidity
definitions.meaning: pH 1, written ..., is extremely acidic on the pH scale

explanation.surface: A Greek person proves extremely sour.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes I as the Roman numeral one, giving pH I.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the twenty-first Greek letter, and pH one marks a very strongly acidic solution.

clue.text: Bill joins fashionable society somewhere in London

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
the ton is an old word for high fashionable society

explanation.surface: Bill enters the smart set in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Acton is a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a suburb in the west of the British capital, so it is a place in the city.

clue.text: Almost the last word in piece of furniture that could be suitable for domestic adaptation

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the furniture

parts.note: a table is a piece of furniture

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: amen is the last word said in a prayer

explanation.surface: A near-final piece of furniture that might suit a home makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last word' is the word said at the end of a prayer; 'Almost' drops its final letter before it goes 'in' the table.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal that can be domesticated, brought to live with people, is one that can be tamed.

clue.text: The fellow deals with clothing at the highest level

parts.note: he refers to a male person
to address a problem is to deal with it

explanation.surface: A man handles outfits for the top tier.
explanation.definitionFit: Hats and similar coverings are clothing for the top of the body, the head.

clue.text: Stir in a little river meeting a great one

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river
the Great Ouse is a major river in eastern England

explanation.surface: Movement in a small stream where it joins a big river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great Ouse is a long river in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir someone is to rouse or awaken them.

clue.text: River swirling round? This may keep you dry

indicators.note: swirling round means turning about, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A river eddying about, and a garment to protect you.
explanation.definitionFit: A raincoat, short for mackintosh, keeps the wearer dry.

clue.text: Unrealistic having new leader that's thick

indicators.note: a new leader means the first letter is swapped for another

parts.note: dreamy means vague and unrealistic

explanation.surface: An impractical outfit gets a new boss who is rather dim.
explanation.walkthrough: The replacement first letter is not clued; crossings supply it.
explanation.definitionFit: A creamy sauce or liquid is rich and thick in consistency.

clue.text: Perched as bird in fixed position guarding last of eggs

indicators.note: guarding means protecting by surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: rooted means fixed firmly in place

indicators.note: last of picks out the final letter of eggs

explanation.surface: A bird sits stock-still on its nest, protecting the final egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds settle on a perch to sleep, which is what roosting means.

clue.text: Weary, having lost heart, and unable to get going

indicators.note: losing the heart removes the central letter of the word

parts.note: weary means tired

explanation.surface: Exhausted and discouraged, someone cannot start.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bound or restricted, as when tied down, leaves one unable to move off.

clue.text: Dying to find relaxation after year's ending

indicators.note: after places the relaxation word following the month

parts.note: December, abbreviated Dec, ends the year
ease is rest and relaxation

explanation.surface: Desperate for a break at the end of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'year's ending' is not the letter R but the last month, DEC.
explanation.definitionFit: Decease is the formal word for death, the act of dying.

clue.text: Fool in failed operation

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the run of the two words

explanation.surface: An idiot involved in a botched mission.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is slang for a stupid person, an idiot.

clue.text: Part of serial publication for children

definitions.meaning: a single edition of a magazine or periodical

explanation.surface: An edition of a magazine aimed at young readers.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine edition is a numbered instalment, and offspring in law are a person's descendants.

clue.text: Brain teaser missing from newspaper? Don't mention it!

definitions.meaning: a paper without its puzzle would have none of that teaser

explanation.surface: A puzzle is absent from the paper, and someone politely brushes off thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are courteous replies telling someone that helping caused no trouble.
